itinerary.title: Arrival at Aswan — Aswan City Tour (High Dam, Philae & Obelisk)
itinerary.desc: Welcome to Aswan! When you arrive at the airport or train station in Aswan, our representative will meet you and transfer you to Luxury Nile Cruise (MS Sara / Oberoi Class). Start your guided visits in Aswan with the Aswan High Dam, followed by a motorboat ride to the island Temple of Philae (Temple of Isis), and the Unfinished Obelisk of Queen Hatshepsut. Embark the cruise to enjoy lunch, afternoon tea, dinner and overnight on board in Aswan.

itinerary.title: Nile Cruise Sailing — Kom Ombo Temple, Edfu Temple & Esna Lock
itinerary.desc: Enjoy breakfast on board while sailing north to Kom Ombo, where you will visit the unique symmetrical double Temple of Kom Ombo dedicated to Sobek the Crocodile God and Horus the Falcon, plus the Crocodile Museum. Sail onward to Edfu to visit the best-preserved Temple of Horus, then continue sailing across Esna Lock toward Luxor with dinner and overnight onboard.

itinerary.title: West Bank & East Bank of Luxor (Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut & Karnak)
itinerary.desc: After breakfast on board, cross to the West Bank of Luxor to explore the royal tombs of the Valley of the Kings, the terraced Temple of Queen Hatshepsut at Deir el-Bahari, and the Colossi of Memnon. After lunch onboard, visit the monumental Karnak Temple and Luxor Temple on the East Bank. Dinner and overnight in Luxor.

itinerary.title: Disembarkation in Luxor / Final Departure or Extension
itinerary.desc: After enjoying your final breakfast and check-out from the cruise at 08:00 AM, our representative will transfer you by private air-conditioned vehicle to Luxor Airport, railway station, or your selected Add-on Program.

sightseeingPlaces.title: Karnak Temple and Luxor Temple
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: Monumental temples, giant columns, and ancient Egyptian history.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: Monumental temples, giant columns, and ancient Egyptian history along the sacred Avenue of Sphinxes.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Walk through 2,000 years of Pharaonic devotion on the East Bank of Luxor (ancient Thebes). Accompanied by your private licensed Egyptologist, explore the vast Temple of Karnak—home to the breathtaking Great Hypostyle Hall of 134 towering sandstone columns, the Sacred Lake, and the obelisks of Queen Hatshepsut—before following the three-kilometer Avenue of Sphinxes to the gracefully proportioned Luxor Temple on the Nile corniche.
itinerarySteps: Private pickup from your Nile cruise dock or hotel in Luxor in an air-conditioned vehicle.
Guided exploration of the Precinct of Amun-Ra at Karnak Temple, the Great Hypostyle Hall, and the Festival Temple of Thutmose III.
Photo stop along the newly restored Avenue of Sphinxes connecting Karnak and Luxor Temples.
Visit to Luxor Temple, including the colossi of Ramesses II, the Court of Amenhotep III, and the Abu Haggag Mosque.
Return transfer to your cruise vessel with bottled mineral water included.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Licensed Egyptologist Guide + Entry Tickets + Transfers

sightseeingPlaces.title: Dandara & Abydos Temple
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: Sacred Temple of Hathor in Dendera with its vivid astronomical ceiling and the masterpiece reliefs of Seti I at Abydos.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: Discover the vivid turquoise astronomical ceiling of Dendera and the finest carved reliefs in Egypt at Abydos.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Venture north of Luxor with your private Egyptologist to two of Upper Egypt’s most awe-inspiring and best-preserved sanctuaries. At Abydos, the sacred cult center of the god Osiris, marvel at the Temple of Seti I—famous for its raised relief carvings that retain their original New Kingdom pigments and the renowned Abydos King List. Continue to Dendera to enter the Greco-Roman Temple of Hathor, where cleaned ceilings reveal vibrant turquoise zodiac constellations, sacred crypts, and rooftop shrines.
itinerarySteps: Morning departure from your Luxor cruise dock or hotel in a private modern air-conditioned vehicle.
Guided visit to the Temple of Seti I at Abydos, exploring the Seven Sacred Chapels, the Osireion, and the Hall of the King List.
Scenic drive along the agricultural Nile valley to Qena / Dendera.
Guided tour of the Temple of Hathor at Dendera, including the vibrant astronomical ceiling, crypts, and panoramic temple roof.
Return transfer to your Nile cruise in Luxor.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Private Vehicle + All Entry Tickets

sightseeingPlaces.title: Valley of the Kings
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: Royal tombs, including the optional tomb of Tutankhamun.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: Royal tombs carved deep into the Theban peaks, including the optional tomb of King Tutankhamun.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Cross to the West Bank of the Nile to enter the royal necropolis of the New Kingdom pharaohs (18th to 20th Dynasties). Beneath the natural pyramid of Al-Qurn mountain lie over 60 rock-cut tombs adorned with luminous scenes from the Book of the Dead, the Amduat, and the Book of Gates. Your private Egyptologist will explain the royal funerary rituals before you descend into three monumental royal tombs, with the option to enter the famous Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62) and Seti I (KV17).
itinerarySteps: Morning pickup from your Nile cruise and crossing to Luxor’s West Bank.
Electric Taftaf train ride to the entrance of the Royal Valley.
In-depth explanation by your private Egyptologist at the architectural scale model.
Guided entry to 3 vivid royal tombs + optional entry to the Tomb of King Tutankhamun.
Return transfer to your vessel in time for lunch.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Valley Ticket (3 Tombs) + Transfers

sightseeingPlaces.title: Temple of Hatshepsut
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: A spectacular terraced temple built into the cliffs.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: A spectacular terraced mortuary temple built directly into the golden limestone cliffs of Deir el-Bahari.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Rising in three colonnaded terraces against the sheer limestone cliffs of Deir el-Bahari, the Mortuary Temple of Queen Hatshepsut (Djeser-Djeseru, "Holy of Holies") is a masterpiece of ancient classical architecture designed by royal architect Senenmut. With your private Egyptologist, examine the finely carved reliefs chronicling the Queen’s divine birth, the transportation of twin obelisks from Aswan, and her legendary maritime trading expedition to the Land of Punt.
itinerarySteps: Private transfer to the amphitheater cliffs of Deir el-Bahari on Luxor’s West Bank.
Walk up the monumental ramps and colonnades with your Egyptologist.
Explore the Punt Colonnade, the Birth Colonnade, the Chapel of Hathor (with cow-headed capitals), and the Chapel of Anubis.
Panoramic photography time overlooking the Theban plain and the Nile valley.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Entry Ticket + Private A/C Transfer

sightseeingPlaces.title: Valley of Queens
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: Sacred necropolis of royal wives, princesses and princes, known in ancient times as Ta-Set-Neferu ("The Place of Beauty").
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: Explore the royal necropolis of New Kingdom queens and princes, including the optional Tomb of Queen Nefertari.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Known to the ancient Egyptians as Ta-Set-Neferu ("The Place of Beauty"), the Valley of the Queens at the southern tip of the Theban hillside holds over 90 tombs belonging to royal wives, princesses, and young princes of the 19th and 20th Dynasties. Your Egyptologist guides you through the vividly painted tombs of Prince Amun-her-khepeshef, Queen Titi, and Prince Khaemwaset, with optional VIP arrangements for the legendary Tomb of Queen Nefertari (beloved wife of Ramesses II).
itinerarySteps: Private A/C transfer from your Nile cruise to the southern Theban hills.
Guided visit to 3 richly painted royal tombs in the Valley of the Queens.
Detailed explanation of royal iconography, protective deities, and color preservation.
Optional add-on arrangement for the Tomb of Queen Nefertari (subject to antiquities availability).
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Entry Tickets + Transfers

sightseeingPlaces.title: Medinet Habu
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: An impressive temple complex on Luxor's West Bank.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: An impressive fortified temple complex of Pharaoh Ramesses III with deeply carved reliefs and original paint.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Often described by Egyptologists as the hidden gem of Luxor’s West Bank, Medinet Habu is the vast mortuary temple complex of Pharaoh Ramesses III (20th Dynasty). Enclosed within a towering mudbrick fortified gate (the Syrian Migdol), its massive sandstone pylons and peristyle courts boast the deepest relief carvings in Egypt—up to six inches deep—along with remarkably intact original blue, gold, and ochre ceiling paint depicting the defeat of the Sea Peoples.
itinerarySteps: Private transfer to the quiet southern edge of the West Bank necropolis.
Enter through the monumental Royal Fortified Gate (Migdol) of Ramesses III.
Explore the First and Second Courts with your Egyptologist, admiring intact painted ceilings and dramatic naval battle scenes.
Visit the adjacent Royal Palace ruins and Sacred Lake before returning to your cruise.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Entry Ticket + Private Transfer

sightseeingPlaces.title: Colossi of Memnon
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: Two enormous statues of Pharaoh Amenhotep III.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: Two enormous 18-meter quartzite statues of Pharaoh Amenhotep III guarding the entrance to the West Bank.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Standing sentinel over the green Theban plains for 3,400 years, the Colossi of Memnon are two twin 720-ton statues of Pharaoh Amenhotep III carved from single blocks of quartzite sandstone quarried near Cairo. In Greco-Roman times, the northern statue became legendary for emitting a musical "singing" sound at dawn, attracting Roman emperors who left Latin and Greek inscriptions on its legs. Your Egyptologist will also show you the ongoing excavations of Amenhotep III’s massive mortuary temple behind them.
itinerarySteps: Private stop at the entrance plain of the Theban Necropolis.
Up-close guided viewing of the 18-meter twin colossi, Queen Tiye and Queen Mutemwiya statues, and Greco-Roman inscriptions.
View the newly raised alabaster and quartzite stelae of Amenhotep III’s Mortuary Temple.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Private Vehicle Stop

sightseeingPlaces.title: Temple of Khnum
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: A temple known for its beautifully decorated ceiling; included on some itineraries.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: A sunken Ptolemaic-Roman temple famous for its newly restored, vibrantly painted astronomical ceiling.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Situated nine meters below the street level of modern Esna—just steps from the famous Esna River Lock—the Temple of Khnum is dedicated to the ram-headed creator god who fashioned humankind on his potter’s wheel. Following a landmark multi-year conservation project, the 24 lotus-and-palm columns and the ceiling of its grand Hypostyle Hall now blaze with their original 2,000-year-old reds, yellows, and turquoise blues depicting ancient Egyptian zodiac signs and sacred constellations.
itinerarySteps: Walk from your moored cruise vessel or dahabiya at Esna through the traditional market street.
Descend the ceremonial staircase into the sunken courtyard of the Temple of Khnum.
Guided tour with your Egyptologist of the newly restored polychrome ceiling, Roman imperial cartouches, and creation texts.
Optional stroll through the historic Wakalat al-Geddawi caravanserai and weavers’ quarter.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Esna Temple Entry Ticket

sightseeingPlaces.title: Temple of Horus
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: One of Egypt's best-preserved ancient temples.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: One of Egypt’s best-preserved ancient temples, dedicated to the falcon god Horus with towering pylons.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Buried beneath desert sand and river silt for centuries, the Ptolemaic Temple of Horus at Edfu (built between 237 and 57 BC) is the most completely preserved temple in all of Egypt. Passing between its 36-meter-high entrance pylons guarded by black granite falcons of Horus, you step into a world where ancient roofs, corridors, perfume laboratories, and the granite Naos (Sanctuary of the Sacred Bark) remain completely intact.
itinerarySteps: Transfer from the Edfu river corniche to the temple plaza by private vehicle or traditional carriage.
Admire the monumental First Pylon depicting Ptolemy XII smiting his foes before Horus and Hathor.
Walk through the Court of Offerings, the two Hypostyle Halls, the ancient Perfume Laboratory, and the Holy of Holies.
View the famous reliefs of the Sacred Drama—the mythical battle between Horus and Seth—with your Egyptologist.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Entry Ticket + Local Transfer

sightseeingPlaces.title: Temple of Kom Ombo
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: A unique double temple dedicated to Sobek and Horus, with a crocodile museum.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: A unique symmetrical double temple overlooking the Nile, dedicated to Sobek and Horus, with a Crocodile Museum.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Dramatically perched on a promontory overlooking a sweeping bend of the Nile, the Temple of Kom Ombo is unique in Egypt for its perfectly symmetrical double design: the southern half is dedicated to Sobek, the crocodile god of fertility and creator of the world, while the northern half honors Haroeris (Horus the Elder), the falcon-headed sky god. Your guided visit includes the famous carved relief of ancient surgical and medical instruments, the sacred nilometer, and the adjacent Crocodile Museum displaying mummified Nile crocodiles.
itinerarySteps: Walk directly from the Kom Ombo river dock up to the riverside temple terrace.
Explore the twin entrances, double hypostyle halls, and twin sanctuaries of Sobek and Haroeris.
Examine the ancient Egyptian calendar, Cleopatra VII reliefs, and the famous Roman-era medical instruments carving.
Visit the air-conditioned Crocodile Museum at the exit before returning to your ship.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Temple & Crocodile Museum Ticket

sightseeingPlaces.title: Philae Temple
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: A beautiful island temple dedicated to the goddess Isis.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: A romantic island sanctuary dedicated to the goddess Isis, reached by private motorboat across the Nile.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Known as the "Pearl of Egypt," the Temple of Philae rises from the granite waters of Agilkia Island between the Old Aswan Dam and the High Dam. Rescued stone by stone in a landmark UNESCO campaign, Philae was the last active bastion of ancient Egyptian religion. Sail across the sapphire waters in a private motorboat with your Egyptologist to explore the Mammisi (Birth House of Horus), the Temple of Isis, and the picturesque Trajan’s Kiosk.
itinerarySteps: Private transfer from your cruise in Aswan to the Marina of Shellal.
Scenic private motorboat ride through the granite boulders to Agilkia Island.
Guided walk through the Outer Colonnades, the First Pylon, the Sanctuary of Isis, and the Kiosk of Emperor Trajan.
Return boat ride and transfer back to your Nile vessel.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Private Motorboat + Entry Ticket

sightseeingPlaces.title: Unfinished Obelisk
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: An enormous unfinished obelisk in an ancient granite quarry.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: An enormous 1,200-ton unfinished obelisk of Queen Hatshepsut in Aswan’s ancient pink granite quarry.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Aswan’s northern quarries supplied the prized pink granite (syenite) used for royal statues, sarcophagi, and obelisks across ancient Egypt. Commissioned by Queen Hatshepsut around 1500 BC, the Unfinished Obelisk would have stood 42 meters tall and weighed nearly 1,200 tons—one-third larger than any Egyptian obelisk ever erected—before a natural flaw appeared in the bedrock. Walk along the quarry walkways as your Egyptologist demonstrates how ancient masons shaped solid granite using dolerite pounding balls.
itinerarySteps: Private A/C transfer to the Northern Granite Quarries of Aswan.
Ascend the panoramic viewing walkway overlooking the 42-meter monolith still attached to the living bedrock.
See ancient mason tool marks, ochre guide lines, and dolerite pounders explained by your Egyptologist.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Quarry Ticket + Private Transfer

sightseeingPlaces.title: Aswan High Dam
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: A major engineering project that transformed the Nile.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: A monumental 20th-century engineering project that tamed the Nile floods and created Lake Nasser.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Constructed between 1960 and 1970 across the Nile south of Aswan, the Aswan High Dam (Al-Sadd Al-Aali) is an engineering marvel measuring 3,830 meters long and 111 meters high. Standing atop the dam crown with your guide, gaze south over the vast blue expanse of Lake Nasser—one of the world’s largest man-made lakes—and north toward the cataracts of the Nile Valley, while visiting the lotus-shaped Friendship Monument.
itinerarySteps: Private drive from Aswan up to the crest of the Aswan High Dam.
Guided explanation of the dam’s hydro-electric turbines, flood control impact, and the UNESCO Nubian salvage campaign.
Panoramic photo stop at the Lotus Tower overlooking Lake Nasser and Kalabsha Temple.
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist Guide + Entry Ticket + Private Transfer

sightseeingPlaces.title: Abu Simbel
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: Abu Simbel Temples: The magnificent temples of Ramses II, usually visited on a separate excursion from Aswan.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: The magnificent rock-cut temples of Pharaoh Ramses II and Queen Nefertari overlooking Lake Nasser.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Carved directly into a sandstone cliff near Egypt’s southern frontier in the 13th century BC, the Twin Temples of Abu Simbel represent the pinnacle of Pharaonic grandeur. Four 20-meter colossi of Ramesses II guard the Great Temple, engineered so the rising sun illuminates its inner sanctuary twice a year, while the neighboring Temple of Hathor honors his beloved Queen Nefertari. Relocated 65 meters higher in the 1960s to save them from Lake Nasser, Abu Simbel is an unforgettable highlight of any Nile voyage.
itinerarySteps: Early morning departure from Aswan by private air-conditioned vehicle (or optional domestic flight upgrade).
Arrive at the shores of Lake Nasser and walk around the mountain dome to the facade of the Great Temple of Ramesses II.
Explore the Great Hypostyle Hall of Osiride pillars, the Battle of Kadesh reliefs, and the inner Sanctuary.
Visit the Small Temple of Queen Nefertari and Hathor before your comfortable return to Aswan.
sightseeingPlaces.duration: Half Day (7 – 8 Hours by Road / 4 Hours by Air)
sightseeingPlaces.guideIncluded: Private Egyptologist + Private A/C Vehicle + Abu Simbel Tickets

sightseeingPlaces.title: Nubian Village
sightseeingPlaces.highlights: Experience Nubian culture, traditional architecture, and local life.
sightseeingPlaces.shortDesc: Sail through the First Cataract islands to experience authentic Nubian culture, brightly painted dome homes, and warm hospitality.
sightseeingPlaces.fullOverview: Cruise by private motorboat or felucca past Elephantine Island and the wildlife reserve of the First Cataract to Gharb Soheil, a vibrant Nubian village on the West Bank of Aswan. Known for its indigo, turquoise, and ochre vaulted-dome houses, Nubia preserves one of the Nile Valley’s oldest living cultures and languages. Stroll through the colourful lanes with your guide, visit a welcoming Nubian family home for fresh karkadeh (hibiscus tea) and homemade bread with honey, and learn about Nubian music, handicrafts, and riverside traditions.
itinerarySteps: Board a private motorboat directly from your cruise dock in Aswan.
Scenic boat ride through the granite islands and birds of the First Cataract Reserve.
Guided walk through the colourful streets and traditional bazaars of Gharb Soheil Nubian Village.
Guest welcome inside an authentic Nubian family house with hibiscus tea, local snacks, and cultural conversation.
Sunset return cruise along the Nile back to your ship.
